title: Variety’s Doc Dreams Live Returns to New York for Third Year
description: Variety is proud to announce the return of Doc Dreams NYC Live, its marquee event dedicated to honoring the art of documentary filmmaking, on Nov.
body:
Variety is proud to announce the return of Doc Dreams NYC Live, its marquee event dedicated to honoring the art of documentary filmmaking, on Nov. 9 in New York City. Following a successful debut in 2024, Doc Dreams will once again bring together acclaimed filmmakers, storytellers and thought leaders for a day of conversations celebrating the power of nonfiction cinema.

	Doc Dreams spotlights the people and projects shaping culture through real stories. Last year’s program featured the year’s most powerful documentaries with filmmakers from “Becoming Led Zeppelin,” “The Age of Disclosure,” “Come See Me in the Good Light,” “Saving Superman” and many more. Their discussions gave audiences an inside look into the creative processes, challenges and cultural significance behind their acclaimed films.
	

	This year’s 2026 edition of Doc Dreams will continue that tradition, convening some of the industry’s most exciting documentary voices. Alex Gibney, director, writer, and producer of “Musk,” will discuss the documentary’s unvarnished analysis of Elon Musk in a keynote conversation with Variety’s Co-Editor-in-Chief and Co-President Ramin Setoodeh.

	The panels will feature:


Ben Kjar, subject, “Standout: The Ben Kjar Story”
Mary Mazzio, writer, director, and producer, “Mighty Mary”
Jana Hojdová & Robert Richardson, director and cinematographer, “Robert Richardson: The White Devil”
Shakiba Adil & Elina Hirvonen, directors, “The Secret Reading Club of Kabul”
Dana Nachman, director, “The Second Life of Freddie Nole”



	The full program of speakers and panels will be announced in the coming weeks, but attendees can expect a dynamic day that celebrates creativity, truth-telling and the impact of nonfiction storytelling in today’s media landscape. Request an invite here: variety.com/docdreams26.

title: Angel Studios Banning Sex Scenes, F-Words and Misuse of God’s Name in Movies
description: Angel Studios is introducing a broad new content policy that bans on-screen sex, nudity, F-words and misusing the name of God. The studio, known fo
body:
Angel Studios is introducing a broad new content policy that bans on-screen sex, nudity, F-words and misusing the name of God. The studio, known for films such as the hit “Sound of Freedom,” will also give its paying members a chance to vote on movies and TV shows to ensure that a majority of members approve of the content.  

	Angel’s co-founder and chief content officer Jeff Harmon announced “The Angel Promise” in a Fox News interview Thursday, explaining why the studio is taking the strong approach. “I think Hollywood generally kind of lives in a bubble. These are excellent craftsmen. They’re the best storytellers in the world. Hollywood has built the best storytelling infrastructure in the world. But at the same time, they’ve kind of drifted more and more away from the values-based audience that they used to serve.”
	

	The new policy introduces three commitments from Angel regarding audience approval of content, strict standards for sex and language and expanded parental controls. 

	“We promise there’s never going to be nudity, and there’ll never be sex on screen,” Harmon said in the video, explaining that Angel is a “faith-friendly studio.” 

	“No sex acts on screen — ever” reads the pledge on the Angel Studios website, “No F words. And no profanity in titles submitted for young kids (12 and under). Angel will not release original films or series that misuse God’s name.”

	Harmon says the Angel Guild numbers approximately 3 million paying members. The new policy requires that films and television series receive a score of at least 70 out of 100 from members to be included in Angel’s programming. 
	

	“This is the first time in history that a major Hollywood studio, or top 10 studio in the United States, has come and said, we’re going to let the audience have a veto right,” Harmon told Fox.

	Angel Studios releases include “Runner, “Young Washington” and “David.” Upcoming titles include “Drummer Boy,” “Angel and the Badman” and “Zero A.D.: The Birth of Christ.”

title: ‘Harry Potter’ Actor Paapa Essiedu ‘Wouldn’t Have Taken This Job On’ If He Couldn’t Handle Snape Casting Backlash: ‘My Priority Is the Work’
description: When HBO released the first-look image of Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape in the upcoming “Harry Potter” series, it became immediately clear that th
body:
When HBO released the first-look image of Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape in the upcoming “Harry Potter” series, it became immediately clear that the show was going for something different. Unlike Alan Rickman’s Snape, Essiedu sports shoulder-length dreadlocks and a more gothic look, swapping the character’s signature buttoned-up robes for a zip-up leather jacket and a flowing, oversized black cloak.“I think the aesthetic is important,” Essiedu told Variety Thursday night at the TIME100 Next Gala, grinning at the suggestion that his Snape was the more stylish of the two adaptations. “I don’t know if style is necessarily at the forefront of my mind when generating the character, but I think the way he looks tells so much about who he is — and who he wants people to think he is. It’s all incredibly well thought through and collaborated with the incredible costume department.”Essiedu previously opened up to The Sunday Times of London about the racially motivated death threats he’s received over his casting as Snape, which he said have “fueled” him to make the character his own. As the series’ Christmas premiere approaches, the actor praised his “Harry Potter” colleagues for supporting him in the wake of the toxic online backlash.“The whole team has been so supportive of me,” Essiedu said. “Obviously, my priority is the work. I wouldn’t take this job on [otherwise], but I walk into it with open eyes. I understand the broad spectrum of what the reaction to what we’re doing means, and I take that mantle on with an open and full heart. I’ve also been blown away by a lot of the support and well-wishes and excitement.”


	Essiedu was honored as one of Time’s 100 rising stars defining the next generation of leadership in business, entertainment, sports, politics, and more in New York City. The actor made a name for himself in the U.K. after becoming the first Black actor to play Hamlet for the Royal Shakespeare Company in 2016, winning the Ian Charleson Award, and subsequently earning two BAFTA nominations for his performances in “I May Destroy You” and “The Lazarus Project.” The “Harry Potter” TV series, which Warner Bros. execs are touting as the “streaming event of the decade,” could be the project that catapults the award-winning actor to international stardom.
	

	“I’m really proud of what I’ve seen so far,” he said. “There are so many people who worked so hard on this project — and who it means so much to. It’s been a long time coming. It’s been a long time that people have been saying a lot of things, and now’s the time for people to engage with what we made.”

	“Harry Potter” Season 1, based on “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone,” will debut on HBO Max Dec. 25.

schema.headline: ‘Harry Potter’ Actor Paapa Essiedu ‘Wouldn’t Have Taken This Job On’ If He Couldn’t Handle Snape Casting Backlash: ‘My Priority Is the Work’

title: ‘Dune’ Movies Returning to Imax Theaters With ‘Dune 3’ Sneak Peek
description:
It’s time to head back to Arrakis and the world of “Dune.”

	Both of Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune” movies will re-released in Imax theaters next month
body:
It’s time to head back to Arrakis and the world of “Dune.”

	Both of Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune” movies will re-released in Imax theaters next month with an exclusive sneak peek at December’s “Dune: Part 3.” A double feature of both movies will hit Imax theaters on Nov. 13 only, with additional showtimes of each blockbuster film from Nov. 14-18.

	“Dune: Part 3” releases in theaters on Dec. 18 and is the long-awaited finale to Villeneuve’s epic sci-fi trilogy, starring Timothee Chalamet, Zendaya, Rebecca Ferguson, Jason Momoa, Florence Pugh, Javier Bardem and more A-listers. The new movie introduces Robert Pattinson as Scytale, shape-shifting villain who attempts to kill and overthrow Chalamet’s space emperor Paul Atreides. Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, the son of star Jason Momoa, and Ida Brooke will play Leto II Atreides and Ghanima Atreides, the twin children of Paul Atreides and Zendaya’s Chani. After appearing in a cameo in “Part 2,” Anya Taylor-Joy will return to play Alia Atreides, the younger sister of Paul. “Part 3” jumps ahead 20 years as Paul has conquered most of the universe and faces new threats.
	

	The first “Dune” movie, released in 2021, was nominated for 10 Oscars and went on to win six, including original score, sound, editing, cinematography, production design and visual effects. It was also up for best picture and adapted screenplay. The 2024 sequel won Oscars for best sound and visual effects out of its five nominations, which again included best picture. Both of the movies have been major box office hits for Warner Bros. and Legendary, with the first movie making $411 million worldwide and “Part 2” growing to $715 million.

title: ‘Union Town,’ ‘Wild Inside’ Among Hamptons Doc Fest Lineup – Film News in Brief
description: The 19th annual Hamptons Doc Fest has announced its full lineup of 40 films, which includes “Union Town,” “Wild Inside” and “Nuisance Bear.”Running
body:
The 19th annual Hamptons Doc Fest has announced its full lineup of 40 films, which includes “Union Town,” “Wild Inside” and “Nuisance Bear.”Running Dec. 3 to Dec. 11, the festival highlights the best non-fiction programming and will open with Barry Avrich’s “Darlene Love: I Know Where I’ve Been,” which is also set to receive the festival’s Art and Inspiration Award. Barnaby Thompson’s “Maverick: The Epic Adventures of David Lean” will close the festival.Filmmaker, writer, philanthropist and activist Abigail E. Disney will receive the Pennebaker Career Achievement Award, while the 2026 Impact Award will be presented to HBO Documentary Films. The festival will also honor “Wild Inside” with the Nancy Neagle Kelley Environmental Award, “Union Town” with the Human Rights Award and “14th” with the Veritas Award.The full lineup is available on the Hamptons Doc Fest website.

	
		Wednesday, Oct. 28 	

	‘Artificial’ to be Honored at SFFILM
	

	Luca Guadagnino’s “Artificial” is set to receive the SF Honors Award, which recognizes bold and innovative filmmaking.

	Guadagnino and stars Andrew Garfield, Yura Borisov and Monica Barbaro will accept the award Nov. 17 at the Bay Area Premiere, where they will also join for a post-screening conversation in the Kanbar Hall theater at the Jewish Community Center of San Francisco.

	“When SF Honors launched in 2016, the goal was to give Bay Area audiences a front-row seat to the boldest filmmaking of the year,” said SFFILM Board President Todd Traina. “A decade later, I’m thrilled that SF Honors will continue for another five years, and there’s no better film to celebrate that commitment than Artificial. This is a story San Francisco is living through in real time, and Luca Guadagnino’s unique vision and style, together with his impeccable cast, give hometown audiences a new way to see it.”

	“Artificial” releases in select theaters Christmas Day and everywhere Jan. 8.
	
		Tuesday Oct. 27	

	Bunny Levine’s Final Film ‘Omi’ Premieres at Austin Film Festival – Watch the Trailer

	“Omi,” which will premiere at the Austin Film Festival on Oct. 30, features Bunny Levine in her final film appearance.
	

	Levine died on Aug. 20 at her home in Tarzana, California at the age of 97.

	“Omi,” a Jewish exorcism comedy, also marks the directorial feature debut for Emily Lerer. Adam Lebowitz-Lockard wrote and stars in the film alongside Dree Hemingway.

	Watch the full trailer here.



	‘Fair Play: The Jordan Chiles Story’ Documentary Set by Campfire Studios and Select EntertainmentAndscape announced Tuesday that production has begun on “Fair Play: The Jordan Chiles Story,” a documentary feature about gymnast and Olympic medalist Jordan Chiles. Directed by Trishtan Williams, the film will be released on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ in the fall of 2027, ahead of the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

	The official logline for the documentary reads: “Bold, joyful, resilient, and unapologetically herself, Chiles has become one of the most recognizable figures in gymnastics and a powerful voice for a new generation of athletes. The film goes beyond the headlines to reveal the woman behind the performances, capturing Chiles at a pivotal moment in her life as she looks toward what comes next, both inside and outside the gym.”

	“My journey in gymnastics has taught me a lot about resilience, perseverance, and the importance of defining success on my own terms,” Chiles said in a statement. “As I work toward LA28, I’m excited to partner with Andscape and Hulu to share more of my story, reflect on the experiences that have shaped me, and explore what it means to step into this next chapter while reclaiming my narrative.”
	
		Monday, Oct. 26	
	
		AFI Fest Announces Grand Jury Award Winners	

	The American Film Institute announced its Grand Jury Prize winners and Special Mentions for the 40th edition of the festival, which ran Oct. 21-25 in Los Angeles.

	“Free Eliza (Notes On An Anatomical Imperfection)” from Alexandra Matheou won the prize for best live action short film. Stephen P. Neary’s “Living With a Visionary” was awarded Best Animated Short Film. “A Woman’s Place is Everywhere” from Fanny Texier was selected as the prizewinner for documentary short film.

	The Special Jury Mentions for live action shorts include “The Bovine Comedy” by Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke for Audacity of Vision, “A Breach Within” by Jean-François Leblanc for Cinematography, “Nobody Said Anything” by Tamara Todorović for Screenwriting and “Mutrion” by Marco Cavazzin for Uniqueness of Expression.

	The Special Jury Mentions for animated shorts included “Emulsion” by Shiyu (Shino) Tang for Craft, “Trading Cards” by Radheya Jang for Story, “The End” by Niki Lindroth von Bahr for Direction and “Saba” by Liron Topaz for World Building.

	The Special Jury Mentions for documentary shorts include “Listen” by Taliesin Black-Brown for Craft, “Water Cooler” by Emma V.F. for Social Impact, “Buckskin” by Mars Verrone for Storytelling and “A Wolf in the Suburbs” by Amélie Hardy for World Building.
	

	The Grand Jury Prize winners for live action, documentary and animated shorts are eligible for Academy Award consideration.

title: The Ultimate Gift for Film Lovers? Criterion’s New Stanley Kubrick Box Set
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	For the f
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	For the film buff who already owns every Criterion release worth having, the boutique home-video distributor has made holiday shopping a little easier this year.

	Released Oct. 20, “The Complete Kubrick” is a sprawling, 30-disc box set featuring all 13 of Stanley Kubrick‘s feature films and three early shorts, restored in 4K. The collection, which carries a $599.95 list price, spans nearly five decades of the director’s career, from his 1952 debut “Fear and Desire” to his final film, the Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman-starring “Eyes Wide Shut” (1999).



						
			
	

	
					

	Among the titles included are some of the most influential films of the 20th century, including the Cold War satire “Dr. Strangelove” (1964), the groundbreaking sci-fi epic “2001: A Space Odyssey” (1968), the dystopian crime drama “A Clockwork Orange” (1971) and the Stephen King adaptation “The Shining” (1980), starring Jack Nicholson. The collection also features the Kirk Douglas-led antiwar drama “Paths of Glory” (1957), the Oscar-winning historical epic “Spartacus” (1960), the Vietnam War film “Full Metal Jacket” (1987) and the period drama “Barry Lyndon” (1975), celebrated for its candlelit cinematography and use of specially adapted lenses.

	For cinephiles interested in the filmmaker’s earlier, lesser-known work, the set includes the noir thriller “The Killing” (1956), the boxing drama “Killer’s Kiss” (1955) and his adaptation of Vladimir Nabokov’s controversial novel “Lolita” (1962). Three documentary shorts — “Day of the Fight,” “Flying Padre” and “The Seafarers” — round out the collection, offering a look at Kubrick’s filmmaking before his transition to Hollywood features.


	Beyond the films themselves, Criterion has assembled more than 25 hours of supplemental material, including documentaries, interviews, screen tests and behind-the-scenes footage. Highlights include a newly restored version of Vivian Kubrick’s documentary “Making ‘The Shining,'” previously unseen screen tests featuring “Lolita” stars James Mason and Sue Lyon, and rare footage from the production of “Full Metal Jacket.” The set also includes Kubrick’s international cut of “The Shining,” which features additional footage not included in the shorter European version.

	New audio commentaries come from filmmaker Lee Unkrich, who edited a book devoted to the making of “The Shining,” and Michael Benson, author of “Space Odyssey: Stanley Kubrick, Arthur C. Clarke, and the Making of a Masterpiece.” Archival interviews feature collaborators and admirers including Douglas, Peter Sellers, George C. Scott, Steven Spielberg and Martin Scorsese.

	The collection is also designed as a display piece, with deluxe packaging modeled after the archival boxes used to store Kubrick’s personal materials. Inside are rare photographs, artwork and documents bearing the director’s handwritten annotations, along with an essay by author and critic Nathaniel Rich.

	Shop the “The Complete Kubrick” on Amazon.

schema.headline: The Ultimate Gift for Film Lovers? Criterion’s New Stanley Kubrick Box Set

title: Inde Navarrette, Jaafar Jackson, Jordan Firstman and More Among SBIFF Virtuosos Honorees
description: The Santa Barbara International Film Festival has announced the recipients of the 2027 Virtuosos Award. The award acknowledges talent whose work in
body:
The Santa Barbara International Film Festival has announced the recipients of the 2027 Virtuosos Award. The award acknowledges talent whose work in films has placed them at the center of the conversation around the year’s most noteworthy cinematic performances. Carrie Coon, Mariana di Girolamo, Rosalind Eleazar, Jordan Firstman, Anthony Ippolito, Jaafar Jackson, Inde Navarrette and Kate O’Flynn are this year’s honorees. The group will attend the 42nd annual event to receive the award and discuss their work on Feb. 7.
	

	“This year’s Virtuosos are a powerhouse group from the most talked-about films of the season. I think it’s especially fitting that so many of them are international performers, and I can’t wait to help welcome them all to Santa Barbara,” Turner Classic Movies host and SBIFF moderator Dave Karger said.

	Coon will be honored for her role in “The Liberation”; Mariana di Girolamo for “Wild Horse Nine”; Rosalind Eleazar for “Misty Green”; Jordan Firstman for “Club Kid”; Anthony Ippolito for “I Play Rocky”; Jaafar Jackson for “Michael”; Inde Navarrette for “Obsession”; Kate O’Flynn for “Tender Loving Care.”

	Honorees over the last six years include Jacob Elordi, Chase Infiniti, Zendaya, Sydney Sweeney, Andrew Scott, Austin Butler, Renate Reinsve, Kieran Culkin, Harris Dickinson and many more.

	The festival will take place from Feb. 3 to 13. Official events, including screenings, filmmaker Q&As, industry panels and celebrity tributes, will be held throughout the city, including at the Arlington Theatre and the recently opened SBIFF Film Center. Recently announced tributes include John Malkovich for the Outstanding Performer of the Year Award and Andrew Garfield for the Maltin Modern Master Award.

title: Conspiracy Drama ‘Hotline’ in the Works at Hulu and Sony From John Swetnam and ‘Spider-Noir’ Boss Steve Lightfoot (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Hulu and Sony Pictures Television are developing a crime drama series titled “Hotline” from John Swetnam and Steve Lightfoot. Paul Shapiro executiv
body:
Hulu and Sony Pictures Television are developing a crime drama series titled “Hotline” from John Swetnam and Steve Lightfoot. Paul Shapiro executive produces the project through his Back East Entertainment banner.

	The official description for “Hotline” reads, “A brilliant yet haunted operator at a top secret criminal call center breaks the rules to help an innocent journalist uncover a vast conspiracy, thrusting her into a deadly game of cat and mouse with the FBI, ruthless hitmen and her own employers.”
	

	Swetnam is the creator of “Hotline,” and serves as co-showrunner with Lightfoot, who is supervising on the project. 

	Swetnam’s best known credits include writing New Line and Warner Bros.’ 2014 found footage disaster film “Into the Storm” and, in the same year, “Step Up: All In,” the fifth and final film in the “Step Up” franchise. He wrote another dance film in 2015’s “Breaking Through,” which he also directed and produced, and wrote the 2013 found footage film “Evidence” as well as Netflix’s 2022 “47 Ronin” sequel “Blade of the 47 Ronin.” On TV, his credits include writing and producing on “True Lies” at CBS in 2023. He is repped by Redefine Entertainment, UTA and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller, Hoberman, LLP.

	Lightfoot most recently served as co-showrunner and executive producer of “Spider-Noir” on MGM+ and Amazon Prime Video. His other showrunning credits include Netflix’s Marvel series “The Punisher,” which ran for two seasons from 2017-2019, Netflix’s 2021 adaptation of the novel “Behind Her Eyes” and the Apple TV’s 2023 adaptation of the novel “Shantaram.” He is also known for his work as a writer and producer on shows like “Hannibal,” “Narcos,” “House of Saddam” and more.

title: Oprah Winfrey, Kristen Bell, Bill Hader and More to Appear in ‘American Valor: A Salute to Our Heroes’ Veterans Day Special
description: The “American Valor: A Salute to Our Heroes” Veterans Day special returns for its 14th year on ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox stations on Saturday, Nov. 14.
body:
The “American Valor: A Salute to Our Heroes” Veterans Day special returns for its 14th year on ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox stations on Saturday, Nov. 14.

	Actor, comedian and U.S. Marine Corps veteran Rob Riggle will host, introducing audiences to a lineup of true stories that honor the courage, sacrifice and legacy of America’s service members. The special, which will be filmed on Nov. 7 in Washington, D.C., is set to feature appearances by Toni Breidinger, Patricia Heaton, Gabriel Luna, Joel McHale and Dean Norris. There will also be narration from Will Arnett, Kristen Bell, Bill Hader, William H. Macy, Chris Pine and Oprah Winfrey.
	

	“‘American Valor’ is about remembering who we are as a nation and who we owe,” Tim Holbert, president of the American Veterans Center and executive producer of “American Valor,” said in a statement. “Two hundred fifty years of America. Eighty-five years since Pearl Harbor. Twenty-five years since September 11th. This year’s program brings together generations of Americans at their best, reminding us of who we are and who we want to be.”

	There will also be a 25th anniversary tribute to the “Band of Brothers” series and a salute to Jimmy Stewart in collaboration with the Nov. 6 release of the biopic “Jimmy.”

	“I’m excited to be back for ‘American Valor’ and to help honor the men and women who have served our country,” Riggle said. “These veterans have incredible stories, and it’s important that we continue to share them and recognize what they’ve given to our country. I’m also proud to be part of this year’s tribute to Jimmy Stewart, who put his career on hold to serve during World War II. His story is another great example of the sacrifices so many Americans have made in service to our country.”

schema.headline: Oprah Winfrey, Kristen Bell, Bill Hader and More to Appear in ‘American Valor: A Salute to Our Heroes’ Veterans Day Special

title: Amazon CEO Says Prime Video Is Profitable and Generates ‘Tens of Billions of Dollars’ Annually; Content Spending Grew 7% in Q3 to $5.9 Billion
description: Amazon‘s stock price is down after the ecommerce giant missed Q3 earnings estimates and ad revenue growth slowed in the quarter — while investors a
body:
Amazon‘s stock price is down after the ecommerce giant missed Q3 earnings estimates and ad revenue growth slowed in the quarter — while investors are rattled by its continued massive investment in AI infrastructure, which put a crimp in free cash flow.

	But on the company’s earnings call, CEO Andy Jassy called out bright spots in the business where Amazon is seeing “momentum,” including Prime Video, which he said is now profitable “in its own right.”
	

	“Prime Video has emerged as a significant business with a revenue run rate in the tens of billions of dollars, now profitable in its own right,” Jassy, who took over as Amazon’s CEO in 2021, told analysts. 

	Jassy continued, “We have momentum with hit shows like ‘Carrie,’ ‘The Summer I Turned Pretty,’ ‘The Boys,’ ‘Off Campus,’ ‘Reacher’ and ‘Fallout.'” Prime Video also has “breakout movies” like Amazon MGM Studios’ “Project Hail Mary,” along with “compelling live sports, including ‘Thursday Night Football,’ off to its best start ever in 2026, NBA on Prime, NASCAR, the Masters and UEFA Champions League soccer.”

	Amazon disclosed in its 10-Q filing for the third quarter that total video and music expense in the period was $5.9 billion, up about 7% from the year-earlier period. For the first nine months of 2026, content spending was up about 20%, to $18.8 billion.

	In its earnings release, Amazon said that its fifth season of “TNF” on Prime Video has averaged 17.7 million viewers through six games, according to Nielsen, a 16% increase over last year’s full-season average. The second season of NBA on Prime attracted more than 2 million viewers in the U.S. during its season-opening doubleheader, more than twice last year’s full-season average, according to Nielsen. The company also said Season 4 of “Reacher” on Prime Video drew 66 million viewers globally in its first 28 days.
	

	Meanwhile, Prime Video series “Carrie,” starring Summer H. Howell as Carrie White (pictured above), premiered Oct. 7 and has generated more than 2.1 billion minutes viewed through Oct. 22, according to data from Luminate.

            During Dyer's first court appearance after his Oct. 29 arrest, prosecutors claimed ... "This case involved the defendant using social media to set up the sexual assault of his girlfriend, the mother of his children, on the co-conspirator's phone."

title: Police Investigating Former Prince Andrew Over Epstein's Visit To Balmoral
description:
Former Prince Andrew
                          Scotland Police Investigating Epstein's Balmoral T
body:
Former Prince Andrew
                          Scotland Police Investigating Epstein's Balmoral Trips ...
                          Amid Trafficking Claim
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 30, 2026
                            7:20 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 30, 2026
                                9:57 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Disgraced former Prince Andrew is now the subject of yet another investigation -- this one into Jeffrey Epstein's visit to Balmoral Castle, the Scottish royal retreat that was a favorite of Queen Elizabeth.
      
    
            Scotland police have confirmed their probe into Epstein's visits to the King's 50,000-acre estate in the Scottish Highlands. Andrew invited Epstein, and the late pedo allegedly trafficked females to Balmoral.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A rep for Police Scotland told multiple outlets ... "We have received information and active inquiries are ongoing but these are at a very early stage. All inquiries are evidence-led, with the needs of victim survivors at the heart of those inquiries. We would never confirm details of ongoing enquiries and it would be inappropriate to comment further."
      

            As you may know ... Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell were both pictured at Balmoral over the years in a trove of pictures released by the Department of Justice.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            We reported earlier ... in a separate investigation, the Thames Valley Police scheduled interviews with members of Virginia Giuffre's family -- including her brother and sister-in-law, Sky and Amanda Roberts.
      
    
            Andrew -- who was stripped of his title by King Charles -- has been accused of having sex with Giuffre multiple times starting when she was just 17. Giuffre died by suicide in 2025.
      
    
            Thames Valley officials have been looking into Andrew's alleged encounter with a woman at Royal Ascot in 2002.
      
    
            Andrew -- who was arrested in February on suspicion of sharing confidential trade reports with Epstein 16 years ago -- has never been criminally charged ... and denies all wrongdoing.

title: Johnny Depp Performs With Aerosmith in Band's First Concert Since 2023
description:
Johnny Depp
                          Walk This Way ...
                          Onto the Hollyw
body:
Johnny Depp
                          Walk This Way ...
                          Onto the Hollywood Bowl Stage With Aerosmith!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 30, 2026
                            8:14 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Johnny Depp's acting career is back on track ... and so is his side hustle as a rockstar ... because he took the stage with Aerosmith at the band's first show since 2023 ... and it's all on video.
      
    
            The star appeared at the Hollywood Bowl with Aerosmith on Thursday ... giving Joe Perry, with whom he's performed alongside as a member of Hollywood Vampires, a big hug when he hit the stage.
      
    
      
      Oh my God! HE’S HERE! JOHNNY DEPP IS IN THE BUILDING! Joe Perry started to talk. I had to turn on my phone and missed the introduction. But he showed up! AND THE CROWD WENT WILD! 🔥
#AerosmithAndFriends #HollywoodBowl https://t.co/1VcTFp9rOI
              @ForeverWyno
          
  
    
            Steven Tyler then blew a few notes on his harmonica ... and Johnny nodded -- telling him he knew the song and was ready to play his guitar.
      

            The crew then played "Train Kept a Rollin'" ... with Johnny flashing a huge grin as he traipsed about the stage.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            It's another sign that Hollywood's embracing Johnny again. He was persona non grata for several years after his trial with Amber Heard. However, fans showed their love for him at Comic-Con in July when he was promoting his new movie "Ebenezer: A Christmas Carol."
      
    
            Steven's had his own legal issues over the past couple of years ... so it's not surprising he and Perry would show Johnny some love and invite him to join them onstage.
      
    
            Johnny was just one of the many stars who took the stage with the legendary rock band.
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            Steven's daughter Liv Tyler and actress Alicia Silverstone -- who starred in Aerosmith's music video "Crazy" back in 1994 -- made an appearance at the event ... as did Axl Rose, Slash, Ann and Nancy Wilson, Dave Grohl, the Black Crowes and many more.
      
    
            Aerosmith retired from touring in 2024 after Steven suffered a serious vocal cord issue, but now they're back. They have another Hollywood Bowl performance scheduled for Sunday ... and don't be surprised if they bring out many more supporting stars!

title: New Jersey Mayor Mocks Resident, Tells Her To 'Get a Job' At Council Meeting
description:
New Jersey Mayor To Resident
                          'Get A Job,' Lady ...
body:
New Jersey Mayor To Resident
                          'Get A Job,' Lady ...
                          And Do You Still Live With Your Parents?
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 30, 2026
                            6:45 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            A New Jersey town council meeting devolved into a chaotic shouting match between a mayor and one of his residents ... with the mayor telling the woman to "get a job" and mocking her living situation.
      
    
            NJ.com published a story Thursday recapping all the drama ... claiming Toms River Mayor Daniel Rodrick personally attacked resident Dana Tormollan over her complaints about him.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Tormollan kicked things off by telling Rodrick she received a letter from him that was attached to her tax documents -- and the letter was full of "political nonsense." She noted, “I told you to stop sending me this crap."
      
    
            That didn't sit well with Mayor Rodrick, who fired back that he never sent anything to her and then asked her, “Did you get a job yet, Dana?"
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Ouch!
      
    
            But Rodrick wasn't done yet. In a mocking tone, he then asked Tormollan ... "Are you still living in the basement at home?"
      
    
            Not backing down, Tormollan replied, "I live in my own house and pay my own bills, so back off, jacka** ... You're a piece of crap. Shut up."
      
    
            The mayor again told Tormollan to "get a job," which got other people in the meeting all riled up, turning the discussion into a shouting match among Rodrich, Tormollan, and almost everyone else.
      
    
            Crazy stuff!!!
